title: Automated Legislative Session Transcription
business: Municipal legislative bodies that must maintain accurate public records of city council meetings.
problem: Manual transcription of multi-speaker council meetings is prohibitively expensive and slow, leading to significant delays in publishing searchable public records.
solution: The pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1 pipeline automates the identification of distinct speakers within audio recordings, allowing downstream speech-to-text engines to attribute dialogue correctly to specific individuals.
steps: Authenticate with Hugging Face to accept user conditions for the speaker-diarization-3.1 model.
Install the pyannote.audio library and configure the pipeline using a valid access token.
Load the meeting audio file, ensuring it is processed as mono audio at 16kHz.
Execute the pipeline to generate an Annotation object containing speaker segments and timestamps.
Export the diarization results to an RTTM file to serve as a temporal map for text transcription.
outcome: A structured, time-stamped log of speaker turns that enables efficient, searchable archival of legislative proceedings.
limitation: The model may struggle with highly overlapped speech or rapid speaker transitions, which can be verified by reviewing the RTTM output for fragmented or misidentified segments.

diagram.description: The flow from raw audio input to structured speaker-labeled output.

code.content:
from pyannote.audio import Pipeline
# Initialize pipeline with auth token
pipeline = Pipeline.from_pretrained("pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1", use_auth_token="TOKEN")
# Process audio and save segments to RTTM
diarization = pipeline("council_meeting.wav")
with open("meeting.rttm", "w") as f:
    diarization.write_rttm(f) # Maps segments to speakers
